summary: This benchmark investigates modular neural transplantation and intermediate interface distillation, demonstrating that a compact 261K-parameter student module can replace a 5.5M-parameter donor branch within a frozen hybrid transformer without accuracy loss on a synthetic register-memory task. The experimental design is thorough, featuring rigorous negative controls, paired bootstrap confidence intervals, and transfer evaluation to an independently initialized host.
strengths: Strong experimental design featuring essential negative controls, including shuffled-target distillation (scoring 6.98%) and untrained branch baselines (scoring 10.11%).
Rigorous statistical reporting using paired 95% bootstrap confidence intervals for both recipient adaptation and student substitution metrics.
Validation of receiver adaptation across distinct random seeds and training histories (seed 101 vs. seed 211).
Precise specification of architecture parameters, token sequence dimensions, batch sizes, and benchmarking execution conditions.
weaknesses: Evaluation is confined to a synthetic instruction language with predefined address masks, leaving generalizability to natural language or vision architectures unverified.
Latency comparisons evaluate only the hybrid configurations against each other rather than benchmarking against an optimized monolithic baseline model.
Submitted under text-only badge without an attached direct artifact bundle, relying on external repository references for verification scripts.
suggestions: Test the interface transplantation and student distillation approach on standard pre-trained LLM tasks, such as KV-cache routing or modular adapter grafting.
Sweep student model capacity across multiple layer widths and depths to characterize the compression-versus-accuracy Pareto frontier.
Include theoretical FLOP counts and peak memory usage alongside empirical wall-clock execution times.

claims.text: The replacement used 95.25% fewer branch weights.
Distillation from intermediate representations has established precedent.
over 20 alternating, warmed, synchronized runs per version on one Apple M5 Ultra (32 programs of 256 tokens per batch)

novelty_vs_existing.title: FitNets: Hints for Thin Deep Nets
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: While FitNets introduced distillation using intermediate representations as hints for training deep/thin student networks, this work specifically tests modular interface replacement by directly slotting a compressed student into a frozen recipient transformer host.
